title: Influence is the derivative second moment
statement: For every dimension $n\ge0$, real-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, and coordinate $i\in[n]$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ equals the uniform expectation of the squared discrete derivative: $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]=\mathbb E[(D_i f)^2]$, where $D_i f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x_{i\leftarrow0})-f(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. For a real cube function $h$, write $D_i h(x)=\tfrac12(h(x_{i\leftarrow0})-h(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $i$ by $b$. Set $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]$ and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$. For every real cube function $h$ and $i\in[n]$, $I_i(h)=\mathbb E[(D_i h)^2]$.
